newsitem.title: FRANCE: French coalition to cap wealth tax for richest.
newsitem.headline: French coalition to cap wealth tax for richest.

text.p: France's ruling centre-right coalition parties agreed on Tuesday to cap wealth tax on the richest taxpayers despite a revolt by backbenchers who say the move is a political liability in times of austerity.

The measure, requested by President Jacques Chirac and approved by the Senate (upper house) but denounced by the Socialist and Communist opposition, would benefit France's 400 biggest fortunes and is aimed at stopping capital flight.

Until this year, the sum payable in wealth tax was limited to a maximum of 80 percent of a taxpayer's annual income. Then the conservative government raised wealth tax by 10 percent and removed the upper ceiling.

Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure told parliament the latter had been counterproductive since top millionaires had chosen to reside outside France for tax purposes. The Senate has proposed an amendment to the 1997 budget restoring the ceiling.

The National Assembly caucuses of both Chirac's Gaullist RPR party and the junior UDF coalition party agreed to support the move in separate votes on Tuesday after what participants described as sharp debate.
